earlier_scan.source_named: King, Julie K. & John Wayne King (eds.) 1984. Languages of Sabah: a survey report (Pacific Linguistics C-78) - survey phonology sketches incl. Upper Kinabatangan

sources.citation: Lobel, Jason William. 2013. Philippine and North Bornean languages: issues in description, subgrouping, and reconstruction. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa (pp. 161-162, 196 fn. 2, 284, abbreviations).
sources.note: No statement for any Sabah language. Sungai Kuamut (an Upper Kinabatangan dialect) example sentences carry Tagalog-style accent marks (fn. 2 p. 196: acute = stressed vowel, circumflex = stressed final vowel + glottal stop): mamalí, namalí, waliyón, inalí, Inaliyán, Iwalí, niwalí, Nakawalí, powalí, Osóy, tuwóy, onó, nantí, Adâ, Apagów (final) vs. sitúri, Walíyò (penult). Data only; the dissertation's stress discussion (8.2.9; Maranao fn. 3 'most languages native to Mindanao and areas further south have lost contrastive stress') concerns Philippine languages.

sources.citation: Smith, Kenneth D. 1984. The languages of Sabah: a tentative lexicostatistical classification. In Julie K. King & John Wayne King (eds.), Languages of Sabah: a survey report, 1-49 (sec. 2.3.9.2.5 'Upper Kinabatangan language', pp. 19-21). Pacific Linguistics C-78. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Nothing. The section gives dialect names (Makiang/Kolobuan/Sinarupa, Sinabu, Rumanau, Gum-Gum Sungai, Dusun Segama, Sungai-Kuamut), village list and lexicostatistic percentages from 15 wordlists; the words 'stress'/'accent' do not occur anywhere in PL-C78. This is the source the earlier scan named; it cannot supply a stress statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid record uppe1427 (dialects kala1392 Kalabuan, maki1248 Makiang, sina1268 Sinabu', dusu1276 Dusun Segama) and Grambank language page uppe1427
sources.note: Nothing; confirms the descriptive bibliography is Spitzack 1993/1988/1985 only (plus King & King 1984 and Ethnologue) and that Grambank has no stress feature.

Spitzack, John A. 1988. Kalabuan clauses. In Charles Peck (ed.), Borneo language studies 1: Sabah syntax papers, 100-148. Language Data, Asian-Pacific Series 14. Dallas: SIL.

sources.note: A full-length phonology of the Sungai Kuamut dialect of Upper Kinabatangan; would supersede a 15-page phonemic sketch on stress (tekanan) and give dialect-specific detail. Likely held in UM's thesis repository (knova.um.edu.my / Pendeta), which is could not be reached by automated download here.

sources.note: The only dedicated phonology of Kalabuan/Upper Kinabatangan; sister chapters in this volume (Lotud, Kimaragang) have explicit stress sections, so this one almost certainly carries the statement. Harvard holds the volume in print (Widener Library (offsite storage) P381.S23 P45 1993; the Harvard library catalogue) - a library scan request for pp. 81-95 would settle the language.
